rules.law_name: Boston Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy
rules.title: Fair chance tenant screening rules for covered Boston housing providers
rules.requirement: Covered housing providers may not use a blanket policy denying housing because of arrests or convictions, and must assess criminal history case by case while excluding specified records such as non-conviction arrests, juvenile records, and convictions more than 5 years old except in limited safety-related circumstances. Agents also may not use an applicant’s credit score to approve or deny housing applications, and may use credit history only in limited circumstances when rental history is unavailable.
rules.key_value: No blanket criminal-history denial; convictions more than 5 years old generally excluded; credit score may not be used to approve or deny

coverage.other_unresolvable: Applies to housing providers receiving Department of Neighborhood Development funding and/or land, providers with income-restricted units created under the BPDA Inclusionary Development Policy, and the Office of Fair Housing and Equity Affirmative Marketing Program.
coverage.summary: The policy applies to certain publicly supported, inclusionary, or affirmative-marketing housing in Boston rather than to all rental housing citywide.

rules.exemptions: Tenant selection limits related to arrests and convictions do not apply where there is a direct relationship between a conviction and the housing sought or an unreasonable risk of substantial harm to others; the guidance does not apply to current criminal behavior; and conflicting federal or state criminal-history requirements preempt the policy.
rules.interaction: The document states that federal or state criminal-history requirements preempt this policy when they conflict, and that the policy is also applied to the Office of Fair Housing and Equity Affirmative Marketing Program.
rules.quoted_span:
Housing providers receiving Department of Neighborhood Development (DND) funding and/or 
land, or that have income restricted units created under the Boston Planning and Development 
Agency (BPDA) Inclusionary Development Policy will not impose a blanket policy that denies 
housing to anyone with arrests and or convictions.
